problem: Prior ObjectNav agents trained with supervised or reinforcement learning on household datasets only handle a closed set of category names and overfit to those environments. Existing zero-shot ObjectNav methods (ZSON, CoW, ESC, L3MVN, PixNav) either still need trained modules or cannot reason explicitly over free-form instructions. These include attribute-specified goals ('bed with the blue mattress') and implicit demands ('I need to lie down').
motivation: Humans give free-form, sometimes ambiguous demands rather than category names, and the target objects may be outside any training vocabulary. Embodied data is scarce, so trained navigators generalize poorly. LLMs and VLMs bring open-vocabulary perception and commonsense reasoning that could support truly training-free, open-set navigation, including in the real world.
key_idea: Chain frozen foundation models into a training-free frontier-exploration loop. GPT-4 proposes target objects from the instruction, GPT-4V discovers new scene objects, Grounded-SAM segments everything into a continually growing confidence-valued top-down semantic map (VSSM), and GPT-4 scores the semantic frontiers of that map to pick where to explore next.
insight: Most of the gain comes from how the LLM is used, not from its size. On an ablation subset (Table 2): asking the LLM to rate each frontier with a [0,1] score instead of picking one directly is worth +5.4 SR (50.0 vs 55.4); CoT prompting adds +3.6; open-vocabulary discovery of scene-specific objects adds +5.4. Swapping GPT-4 for GPT-3.5 costs only 1.8 SR. Failure analysis shows that GPT-4 reduces collision and detection failures but slightly increases exploration timeouts, attributed to more diverse answers.
method: ProposeLLM (GPT-4, gpt-4-1106-preview, CoT): turns the free-form instruction I into proposal objects O_pro with attributes (color, location, etc.) plus a reasoning thought T that is reused later.

DiscoverVLM (GPT-4V, gpt-4-vision-preview): randomly triggered with frequency σ_freq=0.01; lists novel objects O_dis in the current RGB frame and checks whether any of them satisfy the instruction, updating O_pro (e.g., discovers 'tap' for 'wash hands').

PerceptVLM (Grounded-SAM: Grounding DINO boxes + SAM masks): the dot-separated prompt p_t built from O_pro ∪ O_dis ∪ O_pri drives open-set detection and segmentation with confidence scores; confidence threshold is 0.55.

Versatile Semantic Score Map (VSSM): masks are projected with depth and pose into an H×W×(C+2) top-down map (C semantic channels plus occupied and explored channels). Cells hold confidence scores in [0,1] rather than binary labels, and C grows as new objects are discovered, so the map stays updatable.

ReasonLLM frontier scoring (GPT-4, CoT): frontiers are sampled from the VSSM and each is described as 'This area contains A, B and C.'; the LLM rates each frontier in [0,1] given p_t and T. The argmax becomes the goal G_t, re-queried every δ=20 steps. If a proposal object is already on the map, the agent goes to it directly.
FMM planner: a Fast Marching Method policy on the occupancy channel outputs discrete low-level actions toward G_t (forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, look up/down, stop).

setting.backbone: GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview, frozen) for ProposeLLM/ReasonLLM + GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview, frozen) for DiscoverVLM + Grounded-SAM (Grounding DINO + SAM, frozen) for perception; FMM planner
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop, move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/turn_right 30°, look_up/look_down; chosen by an FMM planner toward LLM-selected frontiers
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) + real world (TurtleBot4 with Kinect RGB-D)
setting.privileged: none (standard simulator-provided agent pose used for mapping)

results: On HM3D ObjectNav val (2000 episodes), OpenFMNav reaches 54.9 SR / 0.244 SPL, beating all baselines. It exceeds the strongest baseline, L3MVN+GPT-4 (51.8 / 0.234), and the prior open-set zero-shot SOTA, ESC (38.5 / 0.220), by over 15 points SR. Ablations show that frontier scoring, CoT, and VLM discovery each contribute 3.6–5.4 SR. Real TurtleBot4 demos qualitatively show handling of attribute distractors ('red chair'), out-of-vocabulary objects ('robot arm') and implicit demands.
limitations: Relies on accurate depth and pose to build the 2D map; real-world sensor noise degrades performance.
Depends on closed commercial APIs (GPT-4/GPT-4V), which needs stable internet access and adds latency, so it is not real-time.
Open-set and free-form claims are shown only qualitatively. Quantitative evaluation covers only HM3D's 6 closed categories, and ablations use an unspecified subset.
